title: My anime noir-like detective visual novel
author: soulglider26
selftext:
Big fan of anime from the 1990s/early 2000s, but also noir

I decided to go with many noir style themes, but with anime visuals

I know there's not much gameplay here. As with typical visual novels, it's more about dialogue, making choices, and going with the story.

I live in Tokyo, speak Japanese, and have been making games for a long time. I write short stories and am a big film buff, but haven't written anything long form before so this is my first time.

I've written all the dialogue myself, designed the scenes and the storyboard. It feels a bit more like directing than game design

There's a big mix of AI technologies here, including video, sprites, code, voice models. Many, many generations and iterations.

It's definitely not perfect, still plenty of places I can improve it.

Curious what you all think. Slop?

replies.author: soulglider26
replies.body:
Inspiration is tons of film

Fed a bunch of examples into imagegen to work on art style and characters

Animations are a mix of sprite sheets (image gen) and video (some are kling, some are gemini, some are seedance). That is a long post to talk about getting decent animations and prompting, but there's tons of resources out there to learn this. And the ones for mine are still immersion breaking, not quite good enough.

Then composed them into scenes

Eleven labs v4 voices (this takes a lot of tinkering for emotion and pacing)

Claude 5.5 for help with prompting

Handwritten script, claude + imagegen to storyboard

comments.author: SoMuchMango
comments.body:
Looks good! 

* 00:00 - 00:09 First scene with girl talking is awesome,
* 00:10 - 00:15 These cuts when girl is running breaks the quality, but besides that it is very good. Sequence of hit and running feels very natural,
* Static angry faces of those guys feels like slop (especially this bulky one), focus on better emotions prompts when you have more statists on the screen,

I se a lot of rush in the rest of the animation.

*  Lean guy going down the stairs passes through the bulky guy. 
* Lean guy looks like he is speaking. I think you should let him say something evil to the bulky guy "Finish the job" or something clearly bad. Then give a bit of space and continue narration.
* I don't get what happens from 00:24. It looks like next scenes are not related, but narration continues.

Looks nice, some parts are awesome, but small details breaks immersion. Very interesting project. You may try to find some experienced director/animator/editor to ask for some advice in person. It is not a problem with AI here, as it is quite wisely used.

comments.author: Slow_Yogurtcloset388
comments.body:
looks pretty good. my feedback is to analyze the texture and color palette of the pre-digital anime look. The art style is more of later years of the digital age. It feels a bit too generic. A lot of the line work looks too detailed and crisp. the color palette is desaturated but it feels a bit off, doesn't have the same feel as 90s/early 2000s anime. 

The character design also looks closer late 2010s and on, especially the henchmen. Anime like Patlabor, Akira, Ghost in the Shell, etc the lines weren't as sharp nor the features.

You should be able to get the textured look with using shaders as a filter technique. The rest maybe difficult to prompt.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
Just remember that anime has low frame rate, but it varies between action and talking scenes. I feel you are animating too many frames sometimes, which makes it look like soap opera. One place you can get away with doing LESS.

If this is code and not just animation you can force a lower frame rate on the fly.

Note that even if the animation animates at 8 fps the game itself needs to run at 30+, or else it'll not feel snappy to input.
